chunks: It was narrated to me by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from his father and al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abi al-Jarud from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever recites 'Subhan Allah' without surprise, Allah will create from it a bird having two tongues and two wings, which will glorify Allah on his behalf among the glorifiers until the Day of Resurrection. And the same is true for 'Al-hamdu lillah', 'La ilaha illa Allah', and 'Allahu Akbar'.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Tasbih without surprise?
ai.summary: In Thawab al-A'mal, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the metaphysical potency of Tasbih al-Fatira, noting that reciting these phrases without the 'surprise' (ta'ajjub) of their magnitude transforms the utterance into a tangible, enduring entity. This unique reward underscores the Shia emphasis on the continuity of good deeds (sadaqah jariyah) through divine creation, where a bird perpetually glorifies Allah on behalf of the reciter until the Day of Judgment.
